summary: Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar (1890–1976) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and later as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976).

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held the Seiyu Kiriyama post in Buddhist Studies at SOAS University of London, worked at the Buddhist Institute in 2003, and was attested at Cardiff University in 2002.

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London by 2008 and was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London, as attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Vienna by 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at McGill University, completing a Master of Arts under supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann and teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam V. Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Davidson College and the University of Chicago (PhD), where she was supervised by Paul J. Griffiths and taught by William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1970) and McGill University (~1970–1977), where she later served as Professor (~1978–2017).

Kathleen D. Morrison is a history and archaeology and Indology scholar who studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern (~1992–1995) and was at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen M. Erndl (1954–2017) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974–2023), Ngawang Dhargyey, Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Michigan by 2000, studying under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University (-1986, PhD ~1986–1996) under Alexander W. Macdonald (~1985–1996) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1998).

Katsuhiko Kamimura (1944–2003) was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and later under V. Raghavan, holding positions at Kokugakuin University (~1975–1984) and the University of Tokyo (~1984–2003).
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University (~1964–1968) and served as a Professor at Hanazono University (~1997–2016).

Katsumi Mimaki is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, and Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (~1978–1994) and as Professor (~1994–2011).

Katsumi Okimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1973). He subsequently held posts at Hanazono University as Professor (~1980–2009) and as director (~2009).

Katsutoshi Ono (1905–1988) worked in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and held posts at Kansai University (~1957–1965) and Ryukoku University (~1965–1976).
Kavita Singh (1964–2023) was a scholar in the fields of history and archaeology and Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (~1982–1985) and Panjab University.
